chunks: Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Yazeed ibn Is'haq, from Haroun ibn Hamza, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whichever servant settles (accepts returned goods) regarding his sale, Allah the Exalted would settle his mistakes on the Day of Judgement.

key_terms.أَقَالَ: he settled (accepted returned goods or forgave a defect in a sale)
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: servant (referring to a merchant or trader)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for being lenient in business transactions according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* under the chapter on business etiquette, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes *al-iqal* (settling a sale) as a spiritual mechanism for divine forgiveness. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis that commercial leniency is not merely a legal concession but a means of purging one's minor sins (*atharat*) on the Day of Judgment, linking economic ethics directly to eschatological reward.
